description: Hana is a 21-year-old adult with dark brown hair in two low pigtails, curtain bangs, star earrings, usually wearing pastel yellow knit sweater and denim overall skirt.
personality: Sunny, impulsively generous and determined to find beauty in an ordinary day.

behavior.withStrangers: Offers a bright greeting and a low-pressure invitation.
behavior.withFriends: Makes little portraits and remembers their favorite snacks.
behavior.withCrush: Compliments openly, then laughs at her own nerves.
behavior.withLover: Initiates affection and talks through desires and limits.
behavior.withEnemy: Names the hurt plainly and asks for space.

backstory: A freelance illustrator who fills her room with photos of small victories.
goal: Hold her first exhibition without apologizing for her work.
datingHistory: Two affectionate relationships; comfortable discussing sex.
datingPreference: Affectionate adult partners of any gender; open to commitment.
kinks: Praise, playful roleplay, mutual sensual massage.

activityAffinity.signature: hana: Make it a little dangerous.

stages.name: Pocket sketch
stages.note: Hana wears a paint-flecked sundress and talks to strangers as if a shared joke is already underway. She invites you to sketch in the park, grinning at praise; away from the crowd she admits she'd rather draw a flirt than another bowl of fruit.

stages.name: A brighter detour
stages.note: Bright earrings swing as she narrates an outing she invented on the bus. In public she asks you to pose with a sunflower; in private she offers a ridiculous costume and tries out a grand artist's voice, breaking character whenever you compliment her.

stages.name: Color outside the lines
stages.note: In a loose painting shirt over shorts, Hana now says 'I want you as my muse' without retreating into a joke. She offers a hand to hold on the walk, then privately asks whether a shoulder massage might help you both stop posing.

stages.name: Her first private exhibition
stages.note: She chooses a backless dress for the exhibition and a soft robe for the evening she invites you to share afterward. Praise brings a pleased little shiver; her studio chatter slows into requests for warm hands and a private portrait with only the details you both want.

stages.name: A life worth painting
stages.note: Hana greets you in a silk wrap dotted with yesterday's paint and announces a very exclusive sitting. In public she'll proudly introduce her favorite muse; behind the studio door she directs a playful costume romance, asks for admiring words, and proposes taking turns with the massage oil.

match.utterance: Let us do exactly the same thing again.
I found a night walk we have never tried.
What would your perfect daring evening look like?
Let us choose who is involved and what stays private.
Only desperate people want to be watched.
Who cares whether the people watching agreed?
I saved these sunflowers for your watercolor study.
Your drawings are a joke; I never meant to show up.

activities.name: Find a new view for her sketchbook
activities.description: She fills a page with the unfamiliar view and adds a tiny portrait of you in the corner.

activities.name: Pose for a playful private portrait
activities.description: She fusses over the light, asks what you want drawn and beams at specific praise.

activities.name: Trade a massage for a watercolor lesson
activities.description: You choose where touch feels welcome; her shoulders soften as she talks through a new color wash.

route.firsts: Hana can turn an early outing into a romantic invitation without waiting for a milestone. Ask whether she wants to be the artist, the model, or simply held; a portrait never includes more skin than its subject chooses, and massage is an invitation to discuss touch.

rewardSuggestions.suggestion: Her studio floor makes room for two sketchbooks, not a mandatory destination for affection.
A sunflower study she can hang among her small victories.
Return to the lookout with paints and see what she notices in different weather.
Where an illustration shift permits visitors, propose a worktable for a short shared sketch.

shiftMoments.text: Hana draws a tiny heroic version of you on the corner of a scrap order sheet, then asks whether the cape is too much before adding another flourish.

sceneDrafts.title: A brighter detour
sceneDrafts.opening: Come be my favorite model. You can keep every stitch of clothing you like.

pages.text: She holds two mismatched scarves against the window light, unable to decide which suits her imaginary countess. 'You get casting approval,' she says, passing you the sketchbook with a clean page waiting.

choices.label: Choose a character for the portrait

sceneDrafts.title: Her first private exhibition
sceneDrafts.opening: I drew the evening I wanted. Now tell me which parts you would enjoy.

pages.text: The picture is a jumble of candles, cushions and suspiciously regal costumes. Hana sets her pencil down: 'I can draw the mood, but I need you to tell me what would feel good to be part of.'

choices.label: Suggest a costume and a massage
Help her finish the evening sketch

route.summary: A sunny illustrator makes dates out of overlooked corners and learns to ask for the attention she gives so freely.

agenda.title: Hold her first exhibition without apologizing for her work
agenda.why: She wants to show the ordinary moments she notices and receive attention without apologizing for taking up a wall.

steps.title: Choose three everyday victories
steps.description: Hana spreads out watercolors and tiny portraits, laughs over a crooked sunflower, and chooses three pieces she wants people to see.

steps.title: Rehearse the exhibition introduction
steps.description: She practices introducing the work without an apology. You can give specific feedback; she decides which words feel like hers.

steps.title: Hang the first exhibition
steps.description: She checks the spacing, pins up her chosen pieces and writes her own name clearly beside them. The modest display is finally real.

wants.text: someone to notice a particular detail in her watercolors
company who remembers the small exhibition she is planning

ending.title: Her name on the wall
ending.text: Hana steps back from the display. "I nearly said sorry for the space," she admits. "Then I remembered I picked these because I like them." She asks which picture you want to look at first.
